top_choice_rationale: P001 (B010, Helpman and Melitz) is the one proposal on the slate, and I judge it worth awarding on the merits. Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting generate predictions that representative-firm trade theory does not: exporter premia, entry and exit, and within-industry reallocation after liberalisation. These predictions could have failed, and firm-level data from many countries have tested them for over twenty years, so significance and maturity are not in doubt. Melitz (2003) is the identifiable origin of the mechanism, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus foreign investment justifies a two-name credit. The main cost is credit for precursors outside the pair (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Hopenhayn), and Redding's later quantitative work is also omitted. I would handle that through a narrow citation on selection and reallocation and explicit acknowledgement in the scientific background. The citation should not rest on welfare magnitudes, which are sensitive to distributional assumptions. My literature judgements are from recollection and unverified. The unanimous support among the eleven members is evidence that attribution is stable, not evidence of merit. No award (P000) is ranked second because I judge the contribution clearly sufficient.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for Helpman or Melitz, the only credited names on P001. For transparency: my field is political science, not trade; I am a Stockholm University colleague, in a different department, of Hassler, Krusell and Boppart; and I have co-authored with Torsten Persson, who is credited on B039, which is not on this slate. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
